title: skills for driving buses, taxis, limousines and ride-hailing vehicles

cards.front: What checks should you make before leaving the curb in a passenger vehicle?
cards.back: Look in the side mirror AND over your shoulder to check traffic is clear — don't rely on side mirrors alone. Ensure passengers are not moving around, signal to other drivers, then check over your shoulder again before moving.

cards.front: What hazard can the rear of a bus create when pulling away from the curb?
cards.back: The rear of the bus can swing over the sidewalk and hit pedestrians, cyclists, poles or sign posts near the curb. Also leave enough room on right turns to avoid a collision with the vehicle in the lane beside you.

cards.front: When do public transit buses have the right-of-way to re-enter traffic?
cards.back: When the driver signals to move from the curb lane or bus stop into traffic and the bus displays a yield sign — in areas where the speed limit is less than 60 km/h. The bus driver must still ensure it's safe; other drivers don't have to yield if it's unsafe.

cards.front: What clues help you avoid a collision when passing parked cars?
cards.back: Front wheels turned out; a driver behind the steering wheel; exhaust from a tail pipe; brake lights, back-up lights and turn signals; people walking or children playing near the road. Also watch for doors opening on the traffic side and pedestrians stepping out from between cars.

cards.front: What are the rules for taking on or letting off passengers on the highway (taxi/bus)?
cards.back: Signal to warn traffic you're stopping; stop where other drivers can see your vehicle from at least 85 metres (285 ft) in front and behind; leave at least 3 metres (10 ft) to the left so traffic can pass. Whenever safe, pull off the travel portion of the highway.

cards.front: What are the smoking and alcohol rules for commercial passenger vehicle drivers?
cards.back: It's illegal to smoke in any motor vehicle with any passenger under 16 years old. Don't smoke if passengers are in your vehicle — whether it's moving or not. Don't be under the influence of alcohol while on duty.

cards.front: What must you never do while your passenger vehicle is moving?
cards.back: Collect fares, make change, or take on or let off passengers. Save unnecessary conversation until stopped. You must be able to see clearly ahead, right and left, move your arms and legs at all times, and be ready to reach emergency equipment.

cards.front: How many passengers may sit beside you in a sedan-type vehicle?
cards.back: Up to two passengers on your right side, but only if there's enough room to operate the vehicle safely and only if there are designated seating positions with seatbelts in those positions.

cards.front: When may passengers stand in a commercial passenger vehicle?
cards.back: Only if the vehicle's passenger transportation licence allows standing passengers; the licence limits how many. The standing passenger capacity must be displayed in an easily seen location, and no one may stand where they make it difficult for you to see or move.

cards.front: When may you refuse to transport a passenger?
cards.back: If your vehicle is already carrying the maximum allowed number of passengers, or the passenger is smoking, using profane or offensive language, or acting in a disorderly manner or being offensive to other passengers. If you order someone out, they must be able to disembark safely where they can reasonably find alternate transportation.

cards.front: What are the rules for let-down or jump seats?
cards.back: Under the Passenger Transportation Act you must have a licence or permit before using them. They may be used only in the rear of sedans and only if the manufacturer designed the vehicle to carry them.

cards.front: What are the key rules for transporting people with disabilities?
cards.back: You can't refuse to transport someone just because they have a disability. You must allow service animals (such as guide dogs) with their owners. Speak directly to the person, not their companion; always ask before helping; properly secure wheelchairs, scooters and mobility aids.

cards.front: What is a chauffeur's permit and who issues it?
cards.back: Some municipalities require all limousine and taxi drivers to have one. It's usually issued by the municipal police; you may have to allow a police check and complete a hospitality course (such as the TaxiHost program) first.

cards.front: What are the inside lighting requirements for public passenger vehicles?
cards.back: Vehicles seating more than 12 occupants (including the driver) must have lights that illuminate the passenger aisle behind the driver, kept on between sunset and sunrise. Passenger vehicles must also have a light at each entrance that turns on when the door opens.

cards.front: What inspection documentation must a vehicle with a passenger transportation plate have?
cards.back: If your vehicle is licensed in British Columbia and has a passenger transportation plate, you must ensure it displays a valid commercial vehicle inspection decal and carry the certificate in the vehicle. The vehicle must also be clean and sanitary at all times.

cards.front: What emergency equipment must a commercial passenger vehicle seating more than 10 occupants (including driver) carry?
cards.back: One first-aid kit (meeting WorkSafeBC guidelines), one spare tire, and at least one fire extinguisher. The carrier is responsible for ensuring this equipment is available and in working order. Vehicles seating more than 12 (including driver) also need an emergency exit door or emergency windows; vehicles seating more than 10 passengers must carry warning devices such as flags and flares.

cards.front: What must you do about defects, breakdowns and deficiencies?
cards.back: End the trip if a problem could endanger passenger safety or comfort — fix it or remove the danger before continuing. If a crash or breakdown stops the trip, immediately arrange to have passengers transported to their destination with as little delay as possible. Report any defect that could make the vehicle unsafe in writing to your carrier at the time you find it or by the end of that day.

cards.front: What are the fuelling precautions for passenger vehicles?
cards.back: Don't refuel while the engine is running, the on-board radio is transmitting, or any open flame is present. Keep the fuel nozzle in contact with the filler pipe at all times to ground the connection; if there's a ground strap, connect it to the filler pipe too.

cards.front: How must baggage and cargo be carried on a bus?
cards.back: In properly designed overhead racks (with elastic cord, doors, or a rigid vertical edge half the height of the opening), stowed under seats against a barrier preventing forward movement, in a separate enclosed compartment, or on a passenger's lap. It must never block any aisle or exit, obscure the driver's view, obstruct emergency equipment, or interfere with the driver's arms or legs.

cards.front: What are the key school bus maintenance and cleanliness rules?
cards.back: Test the brakes every day — never operate a school bus unless the brakes are safe. Never transport passengers on a defective school bus; if an inspector or peace officer finds it unfit, it can't operate as a school bus until fixed. Wash the floor with disinfectant solution at least once a week. Refuel only with all passengers off and the engine turned off.

cards.front: What signs and mirrors must a school bus have?
cards.back: Two "School Bus" signs (letters at least 20 cm high, black on yellow) at the front and rear — rear sign immediately above or below the rear window. New school buses need two sets of rear-view mirrors per side, a mirror viewing the entrance door, and a convex mirror at the front to see the roadway immediately in front where passengers may cross.

cards.front: What are the rules for school bus stops (taking on/letting off passengers)?
cards.back: Come to a full stop; have at least 3 metres of road on the left side; be visible to other drivers from at least 60 metres in either direction; passengers enter and leave from the right side only. Use alternating flashing red lights whenever passengers are crossing the road; all drivers must stop for the flashing red lights. Passengers must never stand — all must be seated before the bus moves.

cards.front: What does the law allow and require when operating an emergency vehicle?
cards.back: Ambulance flashing red lights are used only when responding to an emergency call or transporting a patient. You may exceed speed limits and go through red lights or stop signs if you give appropriate warning — use both lights and siren. Before doing so, consider the condition and use of the highway, the amount of traffic on or expected on it, and the seriousness of the emergency.

questions.q: In addition to checking your side mirror, what should you do before leaving the curb?
choices: Sound your horn to warn other traffic
Rely on the interior mirror to confirm the lane is clear
Check over your shoulder that traffic is clear
Flash your headlights at approaching vehicles
questions.explanation: Don't rely on side mirrors alone — look over your shoulder to check that traffic is clear, signal, then check over your shoulder again before moving.

questions.q: The Motor Vehicle Act gives public transit buses the right-of-way when leaving a bus stop in areas where the speed limit is:
choices: Less than 60 km/h
Less than 80 km/h
50 km/h or more
Any speed limit, as long as the yield sign is displayed
questions.explanation: The bus right-of-way rule applies where the speed limit is less than 60 km/h, when the driver signals and the bus displays a yield sign.

questions.q: As a transit bus driver displaying the yield sign, what responsibility do you still have when pulling away from a bus stop?
choices: None — other drivers must always yield to you
You must still ensure it's safe before moving into traffic
You only need to check your mirrors once
You must wait for a gap of at least 85 metres
questions.explanation: The regulation doesn't remove any responsibility from bus drivers — don't assume you have the right-of-way, as other drivers don't have to yield if it's unsafe.

questions.q: Which of the following is a clue that a parked vehicle might pull into traffic?
choices: Its windows are fogged up
Its parking brake is set
Its doors are locked
Its front wheels are turned out
questions.explanation: Clues include front wheels turned out, a driver behind the wheel, exhaust from the tail pipe, and brake, back-up or signal lights.

questions.q: When taking on or letting off passengers on the highway, you must stop where other drivers can see your vehicle from at least what distance in front and behind?
choices: 60 metres
85 metres (285 ft)
100 metres
150 metres
questions.explanation: Stop in a location that allows other drivers to see your vehicle from a distance of at least 85 metres (285 ft) in front and behind.

questions.q: When stopping on a highway to take on or let off passengers, how much space should you leave to the left of your vehicle so traffic can pass?
choices: At least three metres (10 ft)
At least one metre (3 ft)
At least five metres (16 ft)
Half a lane width
questions.explanation: Leave at least three metres (10 ft) to the left of your vehicle so that traffic may pass by.

questions.q: When is it illegal to smoke in any motor vehicle?
choices: Only when the vehicle is in motion
Only in vehicles carrying more than 10 passengers
When there are any passengers under 16 years old
Only when a passenger asks you not to smoke
questions.explanation: It's illegal to smoke in any motor vehicle when there are any passengers under 16 years old, who are especially vulnerable to second-hand smoke.

questions.q: Is it allowable to collect a fare or make change while your vehicle is in motion?
choices: Yes, if the passenger has exact change
Yes, but only when stopped at a red light
Yes, if you keep one hand on the wheel
No — you must not collect fares or make change any time the vehicle is moving
questions.explanation: Any time your vehicle is moving you must not collect fares, make change, or take on or let off passengers — passenger safety is your first priority.

questions.q: In a sedan-type vehicle, how many passengers may sit on your right side in the front seat?
choices: None — the front seat is for the driver only
Up to two, if there's room to operate safely and there are designated seating positions with seatbelts
Up to three, if they are all adults
One only, regardless of seatbelts
questions.explanation: You may have up to two passengers on your right side in a sedan, but only with enough room to operate safely and designated belted seating positions.

questions.q: When may passengers stand while a commercial passenger vehicle is in motion?
choices: Only if the vehicle's passenger transportation licence allows standing passengers
Whenever all seats are full
Any time, as long as they hold a handrail
Never, in any commercial passenger vehicle
questions.explanation: Passengers may not stand while the vehicle is in motion unless the passenger transportation licence allows it; the licence limits the number, which must be displayed in the vehicle.

questions.q: Under which condition may you refuse to transport a paying passenger?
choices: The passenger has a disability
The passenger is travelling with a service animal
The passenger is smoking, using profane language, or acting in a disorderly manner
The trip is shorter than you would like
questions.explanation: You may refuse if the vehicle is already at maximum capacity, or the passenger is smoking, using profane or offensive language, or acting disorderly or offensively to others.

questions.q: Where may let-down or jump seats be used in a passenger vehicle?
choices: In the front seat of any taxi
Anywhere in a limousine
In any vehicle with a passenger transportation plate
Only in the rear of sedans, and only if the manufacturer designed the vehicle to carry them
questions.explanation: Under the Passenger Transportation Act you need a licence or permit to use them, and they may be used only in the rear of sedans designed by the manufacturer to carry them.

questions.q: A passenger who is blind arrives with a guide dog. What must you do?
choices: Ask them to book a specialized vehicle instead
Allow the service animal in your vehicle with its owner
Refuse the trip unless the dog travels in the trunk area
Charge an extra fee for the animal
questions.explanation: You can't refuse to transport a person because of a disability, and you must allow service animals such as guide dogs in your vehicle with their owners.

questions.q: Who usually issues a chauffeur's permit in municipalities that require one?
choices: The municipal police
ICBC
The Passenger Transportation Board
Commercial Vehicle Safety and Enforcement
questions.explanation: Some municipalities require limousine and taxi drivers to have a chauffeur's permit, usually issued by the municipal police, possibly after a police check and a hospitality course such as TaxiHost.

questions.q: When must the interior aisle lights in a public passenger vehicle seating more than 12 occupants be kept on?
choices: Only when passengers are boarding
Whenever the vehicle is in motion
Between the hours of sunset and sunrise
Only when the doors are open
questions.explanation: These lights must be kept on between sunset and sunrise so passengers can move safely in the vehicle; a separate light at each entrance turns on when the door opens.

questions.q: What is the minimum emergency equipment required in a commercial passenger vehicle with a seating capacity of more than 10 occupants, including the driver?
choices: A fire extinguisher and a tow rope
A first-aid kit and a cellular phone
Two fire extinguishers and reflective triangles
One first-aid kit (meeting WorkSafeBC guidelines), one spare tire and at least one fire extinguisher
questions.explanation: Vehicles seating more than 10 occupants including the driver must carry one WorkSafeBC-standard first-aid kit, one spare tire and at least one fire extinguisher.

questions.q: Who is responsible for ensuring a commercial passenger vehicle's emergency equipment is available and in working order?
choices: The passengers
The carrier
ICBC
The municipal police
questions.explanation: The carrier is responsible for ensuring the emergency equipment is available and in working order.

questions.q: Your commercial passenger vehicle breaks down and you cannot continue the trip. What must you do?
choices: Immediately arrange to have your passengers transported to their destination with as little delay as possible
Refund the fares and leave passengers to find their own way
Wait with the vehicle until a mechanic arrives before doing anything else
Continue the trip slowly if the vehicle can still move
questions.explanation: If a crash or breakdown makes it impossible to continue, you must make immediate arrangements to have your passengers transported to their destination with as little delay as possible.

questions.q: Why must you keep the fuel nozzle in contact with the filler pipe while refuelling?
choices: To speed up fuel flow
To prevent fuel theft
To ground the connection
To avoid overfilling the tank
questions.explanation: Keeping the nozzle in contact with the filler pipe grounds the connection; if there's a ground strap, connect it to the filler pipe as well. Never refuel with the engine running, the on-board radio transmitting, or any open flame present.

questions.q: How must you report a defect or deficiency that could make your vehicle unsafe?
choices: Verbally to a peace officer within 48 hours
By noting it in the vehicle log within one week
Only if the vehicle actually breaks down
In writing to the carrier, at the time you find it or by the end of that day
questions.explanation: The report must be made in writing and given to the carrier you work for at the time you find the defect or by the end of that day.

questions.q: How often must you test the brakes on a school bus?
choices: Once a week
Every day
Before each trip carrying passengers
At every scheduled inspection
questions.explanation: Test the brakes on your school bus every day, and don't operate any school bus unless the brakes are safe.

questions.q: What are the requirements for the "School Bus" signs on a school bus?
choices: Two signs, front and rear, with black letters at least 20 cm high on a yellow background
One sign at the rear with red letters at least 15 cm high
Two signs on each side with white letters on a black background
One sign at the front with yellow letters at least 25 cm high
questions.explanation: All school buses must display two "School Bus" signs — letters at least 20 cm high, black on yellow — mounted at the front and rear, with the rear sign immediately above or below the rear window.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the convex mirror at the front of a new school bus?
choices: To watch traffic approaching from behind
To observe passengers seated at the rear of the bus
To give a good view of the roadway immediately in front, to observe passengers crossing in front of the bus
To check the entrance door as passengers board
questions.explanation: The convex mirror at the front gives a good view of the roadway immediately in front of the school bus so you can observe passengers who may be crossing in front of it.

questions.q: Before opening the doors of a school bus to let passengers on or off, which condition must be met?
choices: Other drivers can see your bus from at least 85 metres in either direction
Passengers may exit from either side if traffic is clear
The bus may still be rolling slowly to a stop
Other drivers can see your bus from at least 60 metres in either direction, and passengers use the right side only
questions.explanation: The school bus must be at a full stop, with at least three metres of road on the left, visible from at least 60 metres in either direction, and passengers must enter or leave from the right side only.

questions.q: When operating an ambulance, when are you permitted to use the flashing red lights?
choices: Only when responding to an emergency call or transporting a patient
Whenever you are on duty
Whenever traffic is heavy
Any time you need to get through an intersection quickly
questions.explanation: Ambulance flashing red lights are to be used only when the ambulance is responding to an emergency call or transporting a patient.

questions.q: Before exceeding the speed limit or driving through stop signals in an emergency vehicle, which conditions must you consider?
choices: The time of day, weather and your shift length
Only whether your lights and siren are working
The fuel level and distance to the hospital
The condition and use of the highway, the amount of traffic, and the seriousness of the emergency
questions.explanation: Whenever you exceed speed limits or drive through stop signals, you must consider the condition and use of the highway, the amount of traffic on or expected on it, and the seriousness of the emergency.
